# How to Make Purchases with ChatGPT Wallet, Step by Step (Beginner Guide)

> **In short:** ChatGPT Wallet lets your AI helper pay for things you approve, without the store or the helper ever seeing your real card number. It is rolling out gradually to eligible US ChatGPT Pro users, and every purchase needs your fingerprint or face approval.

Imagine asking an assistant to find a birthday gift, then having it check out for you, but only after you have looked over the item, the total, and the card. That is what this guide covers. By the end, you will know how to add a card, what the bank check is, and how to approve a purchase safely. It is written for anyone who has never used the feature before.

## Before you start

- **A ChatGPT account on the Pro plan.** Pro is a paid plan, so check the official pricing page for current costs. Wallet is rolling out gradually, so even eligible users may not see it yet.
- **Eligibility:** you must be 18 or older, live in the United States, and have a US billing address for your card. The card must be American Express, Chase, Mastercard, or Visa, issued in the US.
- **A supported device** with Face ID or Touch ID for approving purchases, plus your bank's app if your bank asks for verification.
- **Time needed:** about 15 minutes for setup, then a few minutes per purchase.

## Step 1 — Confirm you are eligible and set up an assistant

Before anything else, check the requirements above. Next, make sure you have set up a "dot" in ChatGPT. The help center uses "dot" for the agent that handles tasks for you, and it explains that you need one before you can use Wallet. Look for the option to create or set up an agent in your ChatGPT settings or sidebar, and follow the on-screen steps.

If you do not see Wallet at all, that is normal during a gradual rollout. You can still wait and check back later.

💬 Example: "Help me find a new [item] for [occasion] and get it ready to buy."

You'll know it worked when your dot is set up and you can start a normal conversation with it inside ChatGPT.

## Step 2 — Open Wallet and start adding a card

You have two ways in. The first is to ask your dot directly. Open a conversation with it and type a request to add a card. The second is to use the Settings page: on a phone, open Settings from the left-hand navigation bar, then select Wallet. On a computer, look for Settings in the menu near your account name, then find the Wallet section.

Either way, you will reach a secure form for your card details. If you start a purchase for the first time, the card setup should appear automatically, so don't worry if you land there by accident.

💬 Example: "Help me add a card to Wallet."

You'll know it worked when a secure card form appears, and not a chat box asking you to type your card number.

## Step 3 — Enter your card details in the secure form

Type your card number, expiration date, and security code into the secure form, not into the chat. The help article is firm about this, and it is good advice for any AI tool. For American Express cards, the security code is the 4-digit code on the front. Then read the ChatGPT Wallet terms and the Wallet privacy notice, which are linked near the button you press to save.

Choose the button that adds your card. If you are not sure whether it saved, do not type the card in again. Ask your dot to show your saved cards first, since adding the same card twice can cause confusion.

💬 Example: "Show me my saved cards."

You'll know it worked when you wait for a clear confirmation that the card was added before you start any purchase.

## Step 4 — Complete your bank's verification

Your bank may ask you to verify the card before you can use it. The setup flow will tell you what to do. That might mean entering a verification code, or approving the connection in your bank's app. If you use a Chase card, install the Chase app on your phone and sign in with biometrics first. Only the primary cardholder can add an eligible Chase card, not an authorized user.

If you are on a computer, you may see a QR code. Scan it with your phone, approve in the bank app, then return to Wallet to finish. If your bank's steps look different from what you expect, contact your bank directly. Enter any verification codes only in the secure form, never in chat or in a message to support.

You'll know it worked when the verification finishes and your card shows as ready to use in Wallet.

## Step 5 — Ask your dot to buy something and check the details

Choose what you want, then ask your dot to complete the purchase. When a purchase request appears, slow down and read it. Check the store (merchant), the items, the total, the card that will be charged, and any shipping or recurring-payment terms. A recurring plan means the store may keep your payment details and charge you again on a schedule.

If anything looks wrong, decline the request. Declining is always safe, and you can start over. Nothing is charged until you approve.

💬 Example: "Help me find a new [item] for [occasion], then prepare the checkout."

You'll know it worked when a purchase request appears with the store, items, total, and card clearly listed for you to review.

## Step 6 — Approve with Face ID or Touch ID

When everything looks right, select the approve option and complete biometric verification, which means Face ID or Touch ID on a supported device. Your phone or computer will ask you to confirm with your face or fingerprint. Behind the scenes, Wallet creates a stand-in card number linked to your card, and the store charges that number. Your real card number is never shared with the store or the assistant.

If you cannot approve on your current device, the help article says to follow the link or QR code and continue on a supported device signed in to the same ChatGPT account. After approval, your dot continues checkout and reports the result.

💬 Example: "What was the result of my last purchase?"

You'll know it worked when your dot reports back that checkout continued after your approval. Then check your email from the store for an order confirmation.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake: thinking approval means the order is placed.** Approving finishes your part, but it does not confirm the store accepted the order. *Fix:* look for the merchant's confirmation email or order page before you try again.
- **Mistake: typing card details into the chat.** The help article says to use the secure form only. *Fix:* if you typed numbers into the chat by accident, change your card's security code with your bank and never share codes in a chat.
- **Mistake: approving a subscription without reading it.** Recurring payments can continue after the first purchase. *Fix:* read the recurring-payment terms before you approve, and manage or cancel those charges directly with the merchant.

Wallet also has limits. It can prepare and complete checkout for you, but it cannot cancel a finished order for you, so for cancellations you will need to contact the store.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use Wallet for small, planned purchases, like a gift you have already chosen, and keep your approval habit strict: review first, then approve.
- **For your business or work:** Wallet is set up for personal cards in this rollout, so treat it as a personal tool, and check your company's own spending rules before using any card for work.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with the setup and a practice request, and stop at the review step. Learning to read a purchase request is the most useful skill here.

## Try it now

Open ChatGPT and check whether Wallet appears in your Settings page. If it does, read the Wallet section and the eligibility details. If it does not, ask your dot a shopping question like "Help me find a new [item] for [occasion]" and see what it suggests, without adding a card yet.
